newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India slides in wake of State Bank.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India slides in wake of State Bank.

text.p: Indian global depositary recipts (GDRs) fell on Friday in the wake of the pricing of State Bank of India.
"The market feels dreadful. What has happened is that foreign investors can now only buy the GDR," said one trader.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI fell 2.32 points, or 3.59 percent, to 62.37, with the premium over the local market at 8.22 percent after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 94.50 points, or 2.96 percent, to 3,095.14.
The SBI issue was capped at $369.98 million because the foreign shareholding limit of 20 percent on the stock had been reached, so foreigners became forced sellers of the underlying share in Bombay.
SBI's GDR closed at $14.40/$14.90 after being priced at $14.15 on Thursday.
"SBI is already on a big premium to the banking sector. The GDR will do well because it will be well-supported but any way up is held back by the premium," he said.
The issue was priced at a premium of 4.8 percent to the underlying stock, which closed at 239 rupees on Thursday but fell 11 rupees to 228 on Friday.

The Capel Korea GDR Index ended down 2.31 points, or 3.33 percent, at 67.17, a premium of 27.58 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index dropped 17.58 points, or 2.21 percent, to 776.43.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.12 points at 90.90, a premium of 2.26 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index rose 4.63 points, or 0.07 percent, to 6,616.21
